subject: Defining the request/response contract for chatflow + auth/routing
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@marigold.com>, Marigold Dev Team <dev-team@marigold.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — auth, routing, and response contract (notes + open Qs)

Hi Alex / Marigold team — thanks again for the demo today. Short recap and the outstanding questions we need answered to scope the POC integration: 

What we agreed (recap)
- Redwood will provide an SDK sample to wire auth + routing and a small local test harness. Attachment: redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.md
- Preferred auth: customer prefers OIDC (Okta) with short-lived tokens for calls to Redwood hosted endpoints.
- Routing: primary route -> low-latency chat model for user-facing sessions; fallback -> cheaper completion model for batch jobs.
- Output: we talked about structured tool-calling style for transactions and free-text for conversational followups.

Open questions for Marigold (can you confirm?):
1) Auth binding: will you want us to support token exchange (OIDC -> Redwood token) or do you prefer long-lived API keys managed by your infra team?
2) Embeddings / reranker: you mentioned a semantic search layer — do you plan to host vector DB (we saw Postgres + pgvector) or use your managed vector service? This affects how we recommend reranker pattern (server-side vs client-side).
3) Request/response constraints: what are your expected max user message sizes (token estimates)? Any strict stop-sequence semantics required for the transactional flows?
4) Streaming: for chat sessions do you require partial stream updates to the client (server-sent events / websockets) or are you okay with chunked responses after the model completes?

Initial Redwood recommendations (to unblock the SOW & POC planning)
- Auth: OIDC + short-lived tokens with a simple exchange endpoint. We’ll provide a sample middleware that issues a Redwood API session token with 1 hour TTL.
- Chat vs completions: use chat model for interactive UIs (streaming enabled, default max_tokens per response 512), completions for batch reranking or asynchronous generation with max_tokens tuned per job.
- Tokenization: send messages as chunks; we include a token-estimator in the SDK to warn when approaching budget.
- Streaming semantics: we can support SSE and websocket; SSE recommended for browser clients, websocket for mobile.

Next steps (proposed)
- Marigold to confirm answers to Q1–Q4 above by EOD Friday (13 Aug).
- Redwood to deliver a PR with SDK snippets + response-contract-v1.json by Monday (16 Aug).
- Narrow the POC scope to one chatflow and one reranker flow (SOW draft after Qs answered).

Attachments: redwood-sdk-auth-snippets.md (sample middleware), response-contract-v1.json (draft contract), proposal-quote-v2.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30m if that helps.

—
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Alex Monroe <alex@marigold.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — auth, routing, and response contract (notes + open Qs)

Thanks Soojin — great summary. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Auth binding: will you want us to support token exchange (OIDC -> Redwood token) or do you prefer long-lived API keys managed by your infra team?
We prefer the token exchange pattern. We already have Okta for SSO and would like short-lived sessions. If you can provide sample middleware that handles the exchange, that’s ideal.

> 2) Embeddings / reranker: will you host vector DB or use managed vector service?
We’ll host pgvector on our infra for the POC (we want control). We may switch to a managed vector service later.

> 3) Request/response constraints: expected max user message sizes? stop-sequence semantics?
Most user messages are small (50–200 tokens). For the transactional flows (order creation) we need deterministic end signals — prefer explicit stop tokens like "<END_TXN>" so downstream systems can parse responses reliably.

> 4) Streaming: require partial stream updates?
Yes — we want progressive tokens streaming for the chat UI (SSE in web). For certain backend jobs we will accept non-streaming completions.

We’ll confirm by Friday — I’ll loop in infra if they have followups. Also attaching a short note from our infra: they will expose an Okta OIDC client and can support the token exchange endpoint.

— Alex
Alex Monroe

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — request/response contract details (technical notes)

Nice answers from Alex. A few pragmatic technical points to lock in before we finalize the response_contract_v1: 

1) Stop/tokenization: we should reserve an explicit "end-of-transaction" token (<END_TXN>) for the structured tool-call outputs. SDK will include a sanitizer that appends the stop token for transactional prompts. For chat flows we won’t force-stop tokens but will include stop sequences when a tool call is emitted.

2) Max_tokens policy: set default generation cap to 512 for streaming chat; for the transactional endpoints (order_create, order_update) set max_tokens=256 with enforced stop sequence. We should expose these as per-route overrides in the SDK config.

3) Streaming semantics: implement server-sent events (SSE) for the browser chat UI. Redwood runtime supports chunked partial outputs; we’ll provide an example React hook. For mobile/websocket clients we’ll provide a lightweight WS shim.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern: since Marigold will host pgvector, recommend server-side reranker where the retrieval step returns top-K candidates and Redwood performs an embeddings-based rerank call. Advantage: consistent scoring and reduced client complexity. Attach response-contract-v1.json showing the expected JSON envelope (metadata, tokens_used, reranker_candidates[], tool_calls[]).

5) Auth exchange pattern: will add an auth-exchange example that does OIDC assertion -> Redwood session token. Tokens should be short-lived (1h) and support RBAC claims if you want model-level restrictions.

I’ll create two branches in the repo: one for the SSE chat example and one for the reranker flow. Expected delivery: SDK snippets + response_contract_v1 by Mon (16 Aug).

—Ben

- Reranker precision delta within test set >= 8% vs current baseline.
- End-to-end transaction parsing success > 99% using the <END_TXN> stop token.
